newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slips further, RBI buying continues.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slips further, RBI buying continues.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened to 35.82 per dollar in late afternoon trade on buying by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) coupled with corporate demand, dealers said.
The rupee opened steady at 35.705/710 per dollar.
"It's a combination of factors...RBI buying, import covering, some interbank short-covering," said a foreign bank dealer.
"It looks like sentiment has changed, we saw some import covering today for the near months after quite some time.
"Some banks were also caught short," the dealer added.
Dealers were uncertain of the amount of RBI dollar purchases but said it was "heavy".
"We will be able to hazard a guess in the evening after trade closes," said a dealer.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted at 35.795/805 rupees.
